=== README ===
<!-- markdownlint-disable MD013 -->
# seakarr

Automated Soulseek music downloader with library quality upgrading.

## Features

- **Library quality scanner** — walks your music library directories, reads audio tags (FLAC, MP3, AAC,
  OGG, Opus, WAV, WMA, and more via [lofty](https://crates.io/crates/lofty)), and identifies albums
  whose tracks are in a format outside `filters.allowed_extensions` or fall below the
  configurable bitrate threshold.
- **Upgrade mode** — for each album needing an upgrade, searches the Soulseek network, ranks
  candidates by advertised speed (adjusted by measured-throughput reputation), free-slot bonus, bitrate bonus,
  album-name match and peer reliability, and downloads the best match. The result is written into your
  library when the artist already has a folder under a configured `library.paths` entry, and stays in
  `storage.staging_dir` when it does not; an album selected by `library_upgrade.enabled` is replaced in
  place. An upgrade whose every destination already holds a strictly better file
  keeps those files and still completes the album, so the staging copy is removed without a new file being
  written. A candidate whose files omit the bitrate attribute scores zero on the bitrate bonus once
  `filters.min_bit_rate` is set, so a peer that reports one is preferred; it is still admitted, because its
  real quality is verified after download.
- **Discover mode** — derives the artist list from your library (tags first,
  folder names as the fallback), keeps only the artists that own a folder of
  their own, asks MusicBrainz which conceptual albums each of those is missing,
  and downloads only those. An artist the library only knows as a guest inside
  another artist's folder is skipped, and the run summary reports how many were
  skipped that way; name one explicitly with `--artist` to process it anyway.
  Naming an artist explicitly does not require the library to hold an album for
  it: when a folder named after the artist exists, the artist is processed and
  its albums are placed into that folder, and when there is neither an album nor
  a folder the run warns and keeps the downloads in staging.
  Albums already present are never
  searched or re-downloaded, and each run stops after
  `discover.max_cycle_downloads` download attempts so a large library fills in
  over successive runs. Release types come from `discography.allowed_types`.
- **Manual & batch modes** — search for a specific artist/album on demand, or process a newline-separated
  text file of `artist - album` lines to download a curated wantlist.
  A run places each completed album into the artist's existing library folder when one exists
  anywhere under a configured `library.paths` entry; when the artist has no folder there, or the
  album's destination folder already exists, a manual run keeps the download in
  `storage.staging_dir` (batch and upgrade runs merge into the existing folder instead, keeping
  any file that already parses as audio). An
  album-only request names no artist, so it always stays in staging and says nothing: only manual
  mode can express one, because upgrade mode rejects `--album` on its own and a batch line is trimmed
  before it is parsed, so a line written as `" - Album"` is read as an artist-only line. An artist-naming run with a configured library path explains a
  staging-only download once it has one.
- **Authoritative artist discography** — artist-only manual runs resolve conceptual albums from MusicBrainz
  release groups (cached locally for 30 days) and then run one sequential `Artist Album` Soulseek search per
  eligible album, oldest first. The same authoritative resolution powers `discover` mode for every artist
  it sweeps — those that own a folder named after them. Release categories and optional MusicBrainz artist IDs are configurable; the
  previous folder heuristic remains the explicit opt-out and the visible fallback.
- **Quality filtering** — filter Soulseek results by file extension, minimum
  bitrate, excluded keywords, and upload availability. With
  `download.max_queue_length: 0` a peer must offer a free upload slot; a
  positive limit also admits zero-slot peers until their reported queue
  position can be validated. Path-traversal names are rejected.
- **Peer reputation** — remembers each peer's effective throughput (bytes ÷ transfer time: retry delays plus
  the final transfer, excluding queue wait) and success rate (in SQLite), and ranks search results by a blend
  of advertised and measured throughput plus a reliability factor, so fast, reliable peers are preferred and
  slow or error-prone peers are demoted — regardless of what you search for. Controlled by

# Nested staging album layout

## Problem

A staged album is one directory named `<artist>--<album>` directly under
`storage.staging_dir`, so a download that stays in staging reads as
`downloads/staging/Artist Name--Album Name/01 - Track.flac`. The operator wants the
two components to be real directories instead:
`downloads/staging/Artist Name/Album Name/01 - Track.flac`.

The flattened name is not only cosmetic. It is a lossy encoding of two values into one
path component, and the code that consumes it has to decode it again:

| Site | Behaviour today |
| --- | --- |
| `src/runner.rs:508-516` | Builds `format!("{}--{}", artist.replace(['/','\\'], "-"), album.unwrap_or("unknown").replace(['/','\\'], "-"))` and joins it to the staging root. |
| `src/organizer.rs:516-533` `disc_subdir` | Walks a staged file's parent directories and stops when a directory name `.contains("--")`, because that names the album staging root. An album whose own name contains `--` cannot be told from a boundary by this test. |
| `src/organizer.rs:758-763` `parse_album_slug` | Splits on the first `--` to recover `(artist, album)`; a name without a separator becomes album `"Unknown"`. |
| `src/organizer.rs:774-810` `recover_interrupted_upgrades` | Reads the top level of the staging root, treats every directory as an album slug, re-verifies a `success` album by copying it back, and deletes every other leftover. |
| `src/runner.rs:355-389` `discard_refused_staging` | Removes a refused album's staged files, then prunes directories that are now empty. Its warnings explain the `A--B` + `C` versus `A` + `B--C` slug collapse. |
| `src/runner.rs:392-413` `finish_library_write` | Removes the album staging directory after the album has been written to the library. |

# Nested staging album layout Implementation Plan

> **For agentic workers:** REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use sub-agents (recommended) to implement this plan task-by-task. Steps use checkbox (`- [ ]`) syntax for tracking.

**Goal:** Stage every download under `<storage.staging_dir>/<artist>/<album>/` instead of `<storage.staging_dir>/<artist>--<album>/`, migrating existing legacy directories on startup.

**Architecture:** A new `src/staging.rs` owns the layout rule (`artist_dir`, `album_dir`), the startup migration (`normalise_layout`, `prepare`) and the staging scan (`scan`, which resolves a sanitised directory name back to the raw `processed_albums` row). `organizer.rs` keeps the sanitiser and the library half of recovery; `runner.rs` and `main.rs` call `staging::prepare` from each mode entry point and derive every album staging path from `staging::album_dir`.

**Tech Stack:** Rust 2024, `rusqlite` (SQLite), `tokio`, `tracing`, `tempfile` for tests. No new dependency.

**Spec:** `docs/agent/specs/2026-10-08-nested-staging-album-layout-design.md` (approved, commit `542309e`).

> **Plan location note:** the invoking chain asked for `docs/plans/`. The repository convention (`AGENTS.md` rule 7, and every plan since `docs/agent/plans/2026-09-09-queue-aware-download-timeouts.md`) is `docs/agent/plans/`. This plan follows the repository convention; `docs/plans/` is a legacy directory holding pre-convention plans only.

---

## Scope Check

Single subsystem. The spec changes the staging path layout in one crate, with one new module. It is not separable into independent plans: the construction site, the decode sites, the migration and the recovery lookup must land together or staging holds two layouts at once and recovery deletes real albums as debris. **No split.**

## File Structure

| File | Responsibility after this change |
| --- | --- |
| `src/staging.rs` (new) | The staging layout rule, the legacy migration, and the staging scan with identity resolution. |
| `src/lib.rs` (modify) | Declare `pub mod staging;`. |
| `src/organizer.rs` (modify) | Keeps `sanitize_component`, `parse_album_slug` (legacy parser), `resume_library_upgrade`. `disc_subdir` gains an album-component parameter; `recover_interrupted_upgrades` iterates `staging::scan`. |
| `src/runner.rs` (modify) | `process_album_internal` builds the nested album path; `finish_library_write` and `discard_refused_staging` prune the artist level; three mode entry points call `staging::prepare`. |
| `src/main.rs` (modify) | `run_batch_mode` calls `staging::prepare`. |
| `src/download.rs` (modify) | One added test assertion only. Production code unchanged. |
| `tests/pipeline_test.rs` (modify) | The end-to-end staging fixture expects the nested tree. |

Order matters: Tasks 1-5 build `staging.rs` with no production caller, so the suite stays green. Task 6 changes `disc_subdir` (its one caller is updated in the same task). Task 7 switches recovery over. Task 8 switches the runner and sweeps the runner test fixtures. Task 9 wires the mode entry points. Task 10 finishes the end-to-end and documentation work.

🖥️ Harness: pi.

No `Project context status: loaded.` marker existed in this conversation (only `Harness status: loaded.`), so gathering context.

## Context synthesis — seakarr

- **What it is** — `/data/seakarr`, a Rust CLI crate (`seakarr`, **v0.33.1**) that scans a music library for weak/absent albums, searches Soulseek, downloads, and places or upgrades them. Four modes: `upgrade` (ex-`auto`), `discover` (MusicBrainz gap-filling), `manual`, `batch`. Branch `main`, HEAD `0188e18 chore: bump version to 0.33.1`, working tree clean and in sync with `origin/main`.

- **Last landed work** — two arcs, both shipped: `0.33.0` **nested staging layout** (`<staging>/<artist>/<album>/` replacing the lossy `<artist>--<album>` slug; new `src/staging.rs` owns the layout rule, a one-way legacy migration and staging scan/recovery identity), then `0.33.1` **MusicBrainz rate-limit honouring** (`ef7373d`: pause inside a `Retry-After`/503 window instead of retrying through it). Before that: `0.32.0` artist identification by IPI/ISNI/MBID in `--artist`.

- **Relevant existing architecture for this request** — `discover` is library-driven: `src/discover.rs` builds an artist index from the library (tags first, folder names fallback), then `src/discography/` (`mod.rs`, `musicbrainz.rs`, `bundle.rs`, `identifier.rs`) resolves conceptual albums from MusicBrainz **release groups**, cached locally for 30 days, filtered by `discography.allowed_types`. Downloads are per eligible album, oldest first, capped by `discover.max_cycle_downloads`. There is currently **no label/label-id concept anywhere in `src/`** — no config key, no query parameter, no CLI flag. Label-based discovery would be a genuinely new data path, not a variation of the existing artist sweep.

- **CLI shape** — `clap` v4 with `derive`, overridden by a hand-written validator in `src/mode.rs` that produces `ExecutionPlan::{Upgrade, Manual{artist,album}, Batch{file}, Discover{artist}}` plus `CliOverrides`. Every cross-mode incompatibility (`--album` vs discover, `--batch-file` vs discover, blank values) is rejected there with a specific message, and there are dedicated tests (`tests/mode_resolution_test.rs`, `tests/schedule_cli_test.rs`). A new `--label` flag means touching the clap struct, the overrides struct, `mode.rs` validation (including the discover-vs-other-mode conflict matrix), and those test files.

- **Repo conventions the coming spec must obey** — non-trivial changes land as a **spec + plan pair** under `docs/agent/specs/` and `docs/agent/plans/` (20 specs, 17 plans so far; legacy `docs/specs|plans` are superseded and must not be used), strict TDD with a genuine RED phase, two distinct reviewer models, cognitive-complexity ceiling 25, and a Rust gate set with a **95% line-coverage floor** (current 97.12%). Historical specs are annotated with dated corrections rather than rewritten.

- **Gate residue to be aware of** — the `0.33.0` release ran seven review rounds and the operator overrode the circuit breaker; those round-7 fixes are test-covered but were never re-read by a reviewer. `docs/agent/reviews/` **does not exist**, so there are zero residual review ledgers and no recorded pending findings. `REVIEW_TRIAGE_STATUS: NONE`.

- **Known behaviour of the abort path, from the last session** — a discover run terminates with `musicbrainz error: … 3 consecutive MusicBrainz failures; aborting discover run` (`DISCOVER_PROVIDER_FAILURE_LIMIT = 3` in `src/runner.rs`). Any label-driven flow that queries MusicBrainz will inherit that failure counter, the 503 handling and the stale-cache behaviour, so the spec must say how label resolution interacts with them.

- **Environment footgun** — the host exposes the library as `/mnt/user/Music/...` while containers see `/media/Music/...`; placement decisions must be judged against configured `library.paths` prefixes, not the shell CWD.

The open design questions I will put to you with structured options once the chain reaches design — chiefly: how the label is named (free-text vs MusicBrainz label ID), whether label discovery is additive to or a replacement for the library-derived artist sweep, how "new" is defined (ignore-processed vs a release-date cutoff), whether artist folders are created for label-sourced albums that the library does not hold, and whether `discography.allowed_types` is reused for the `<type wanted>` selector or a second key is introduced.

The MusicBrainz API search requests provide a way to search for MusicBrainz entities based on different sorts of queries. The results are returned in either XML (matching the [MMD](/doc/MusicBrainz_XML_Meta_Data)) or JSON format, and are provided by a [search server](/doc/Search_Server) built using Lucene technology.

This sections lists the parameters common to all resources.

**type**

Selects the entity index to be searched: annotation, area, artist, cdstub, event, instrument, label, place, recording, release, release-group, series, tag, work, url

**fmt**

Selects the representation of the results. Defaults to `xml`, but can also be set to `json`.

**query**

Lucene search query. This is mandatory

**limit**

An integer value defining how many entries should be returned. Only values between 1 and 100 (both inclusive) are allowed. If not given, this defaults to 25.

**offset**

Return search results starting at a given offset. Used for paging through more than one page of results.

**dismax**

If set to "true", switches the Solr query parser from edismax to [dismax](https://lucene.apache.org/solr/guide/6_6/the-dismax-query-parser.html), which will escape certain special query syntax characters by default for ease of use. This is equivalent to switching from the "Indexed search with advanced query syntax" method to the plain "Indexed search" method on the website. Defaults to "false".

**version**

[MMD](/doc/MusicBrainz_XML_Meta_Data) version, defaults to 2, version 1 is no longer supported since [search overhaul in 2018](https://blog.metabrainz.org/2018/06/15/musicbrainz-search-overhaul/).

  
The query field supports the full Lucene Search syntax; you can find a detailed guide at [Lucene Search Syntax](https://lucene.apache.org/core/7_7_2/queryparser/org/apache/lucene/queryparser/classic/package-summary.html#package.description). For example, you can set conditions while searching for a name with the AND operator.

Example: [https://musicbrainz.org/ws/2/recording?query=%22we%20will%20rock%20you%22%20AND%20arid:0383dadf-2a4e-4d10-a46a-e9e041da8eb3](https://musicbrainz.org/ws/2/recording?query=%22we%20will%20rock%20you%22%20AND%20arid:0383dadf-2a4e-4d10-a46a-e9e041da8eb3) will find any recordings of "We Will Rock You" by Queen.

  
To search for fields that are unknown or null, use the following syntax -

\-search\_field:\*

Example: For releases with no format set can be searched via: [\-format:\*](https://musicbrainz.org/search?query=-format%3A*&type=release&limit=25&method=advanced)

  
Numeric count based fields can be searched for by looking for 0

Example: [https://musicbrainz.org/ws/2/release-group/?query=releases:0](https://musicbrainz.org/ws/2/release-group/?query=releases:0)

  
To perform a literal search, you'll need to [escape characters special to Lucene](https://lucene.apache.org/core/4_3_0/queryparser/org/apache/lucene/queryparser/classic/package-summary.html#Escaping_Special_Characters). This is in addition to any URL encoding.

Example: [https://musicbrainz.org/ws/2/artist/?query=ac%5C%2Fdc](https://musicbrainz.org/ws/2/artist/?query=ac%5C%2Fdc)

content.text:
I've finished exploring. Relevant findings before the first question:

- `discover` today is strictly **library-driven**: `src/discover.rs` derives artist keys from tags/folder names, then `src/discography/musicbrainz.rs` resolves each artist and calls `/ws/2/release-group?artist=<mbid>` (paginated, `release-group-count` guard `MAX_RELEASE_GROUPS`, 30-day SQLite cache keyed by artist name → `discography_cache`).
- MusicBrainz **cannot** browse release-groups by label. The working path is browse **releases** by label: `/ws/2/release?label=<mbid>&type=album&status=official&inc=release-groups` — each release carries its release-group inline (`id`, `title`, `primary-type`, `secondary-types`, `first-release-date`), so `AlbumTarget`/`select_albums`/`release_allowed` can be reused unchanged.
- Probed live: `label:"Hospital Records"` returns **5** labels (score 100 = UK drum & bass / label code 12939; 62 = US noisecore). Its releases: **1137** total, **397** with `type=album&status=official` (4 pages at 100/page).
- There is **no** label concept anywhere in `src/` — no config key, no CLI flag, no query param. No new dependency is needed.

options.description: Mirrors the existing --artist flag, which already accepts a name, IPI, ISNI or MBID. A UUID-shaped value is a direct MBID lookup; anything else is a MusicBrainz label search resolved with the same exact-match + score-dominance safety rules as artists. One flag to document and test.
options.label: One --label value, name or MBID (Recommended)
options.preview:
seakarr --mode discover --label "Hospital Records"
seakarr --mode discover --label 8562598d-60d1-4bd6-8b85-4d709e951770

# plus optional pinning, like discography.artist_mbids:
discography:
  label_mbids:
    "Hospital Records": 8562598d-60d1-4bd6-8b85-4d709e951770

options.description: Explicit split: --label takes a free-text name and is always resolved via search; --label-id takes a MusicBrainz UUID and skips resolution entirely. Clearer errors, but two flags to validate, document and test, and an inconsistency with how --artist already behaves.
options.label: Two flags: --label and --label-id
options.preview:
seakarr --mode discover --label "Hospital Records"
seakarr --mode discover --label-id 8562598d-60d1-4bd6-8b85-4d709e951770

# rejecting both at once:
# --label and --label-id are mutually exclusive

options.description: Smallest surface: --label is always a name resolved by search. When MusicBrainz returns several plausible labels the run stops and prints the candidates, and the operator disambiguates by choosing a more specific name. No MBID path at all — awkward for genuinely ambiguous labels.
options.label: Name only, ambiguous names fail
options.preview:

# error:
# label could not be resolved safely: 5 candidates match
# "hospital records": Hospital Records (UK drum & bass, score 100),
# Hospital Records (US noisecore, score 62), ...

options.description: Label runs use discography.allowed_types by default (today: StudioAlbum only), and --release-type album,ep,single... overrides it for that run. content.text:
# Design: label-based discovery

## 1. Goal and scope

Add a **label sweep** to `discover` mode: `--label` names one or more record labels (comma-delimited), MusicBrainz resolves each to a label entity, and every release group of the **wanted type** on that label is downloaded unless the library already holds it. Nothing about the existing library-derived artist sweep changes.

In scope: label identity resolution, catalogue retrieval with caching, work-list assembly, staging-only download, run reporting, CLI/config surface.
Out of scope (YAGNI): per-label quality overrides, label→artist "follow the roster" tracking beyond that label's releases, writing into the library, a new release-notification channel.

## 2. CLI and config surface

| Surface | Shape | Rule |
|---|---|---|
| `--label` | `Option<Vec<String>>`, `value_delimiter = ','`, repeatable | Each element is a label **name or MusicBrainz label MBID**. Only valid with `--mode discover`. Blank element → error. Two elements normalising to the same key → error. |
| `--release-type` | `Option<Vec<String>>`, `value_delimiter = ','` | Overrides `discography.allowed_types` for this run. Accepted values are the `DiscographyReleaseType` snake_case names, plus `album` as a documented alias of `studio_album`. Unknown value → error naming the accepted set. Requires `--label`. |
| `--since` | `Option<String>` | `YYYY`, `YYYY-MM` or `YYYY-MM-DD`, validated by the existing partial-date rules. Lower bound on the release group's first-release-date. Requires `--label`. |
| `discography.label_mbids` | `BTreeMap<String, String>` | Pinned label name → MBID, exactly like `artist_mbids`: keys non-empty and unique after normalisation, values valid MBIDs. A pin wins over search. |

Mutual exclusions, each with its own message: `--label` with `--artist`; `--label` outside discover; `--release-type`/`--since` without `--label`; `--label` with `--album`/`--batch-file`. `--ignore-processed`, `--library-path`, `--schedule` keep working unchanged.

`--release-type` and `--since` are **runtime-only**. They ride on the execution plan, not on `Config`:

```rust
ExecutionPlan::Discover {
    artist: Option<String>,
    labels: Vec<LabelRequest>,          // empty = library sweep
    release_types: Option<Vec<DiscographyReleaseType>>,
    since: Option<PartialDate>,
}
```

## 3. Label identity resolution

`src/discography/label.rs` mirrors `identifier.rs`: `LabelInput::parse(&str)` classifies each value as `Mbid` or `Name`, `validate()` rejects a malformed UUID shape before any request, and `cache_key()`/`pin_key()` give the `label:` namespaced key.

Resolution reuses the artist dominance rules rather than inventing weaker ones, because the probe showed they are needed — `label:"Hospital Records"` returns five candidates, scores 100 and 62 among them:

1. A pinned `discography.label_mbids` entry wins and is fetched by ID.
2. An MBID-shaped value is looked up by ID (`/ws/2/label/<mbid>`).
3. A name is searched (`/ws/2/label?query=label:"<name>"`). Exactly one canonical exact-name match is accepted; duplicates require every candidate to carry a score, exactly one top score at `REQUIRED_TOP_SCORE`, and a lead of at least `REQUIRED_SCORE_MARGIN` over the runner-up. Otherwise `LabelUnresolved` with the candidate list in the message.
4. The resolved label's canonical name and MBID are what the summary reports, so the operator can see which label was chosen.

New error variants: `DiscographyError::LabelUnresolved(String)` and `LabelSearchInconsistent(String)`. Both classify as `DiscoveryFailure::Unresolved` (a name that will not resolve must not trip the outage breaker); `LabelUnresolved` is added to `is_stable_artist_resolution_failure` so a hopeless name is remembered in `discography_failures` under `label:<key>` for `failure_cache_days`.

## 4. Catalogue retrieval and cache

MusicBrainz cannot browse release **groups** by label, so the sweep browses **releases** and reads each release's inline release group:

```
GET /ws/2/release?label=<mbid>&status=official&inc=release-groups&fmt=json&limit=100&offset=N
```

- `status=official` is sent server-side: it removes bootlegs and promotional duplicates with no client-side guesswork.
- `type` is deliberately **not** sent. Browse type filtering cannot express secondary types (`live`, `compilation`, `remix`, `soundtrack`, `dj mix`, `mixtape`), so a conditional parameter would make the server and `release_allowed` two sources of truth. `release_allowed` stays the only classifier. Accepted cost, measured on the real label: Hospital Records has 1137 official releases (12 pages) versus 397 with `type=album` (4 pages). Paid once per cache lifetime.
- Pagination guards mirror `release_groups`: first page offset must be 0, each page's `release-count` must equal the first, each page length must equal `min(remaining, 100)`, no duplicate release IDs, and `MAX_LABEL_RELEASES = 5000` aborts with `IncompletePagination` rather than silently truncating. A partial catalogue is never treated as complete, because an incomplete label catalogue would look exactly like "nothing new".
- The stalled-response, 4 MiB body cap, `Retry-After`/503 pause handling and rate limiting are the existing provider plumbing — unchanged.

Caching, per your choice, reuses `discography_cache` with no schema migration:

| Column | Value |
|---|---|
| `artist_key` | `label:<pin_key(label name)>` |
| `artist_mbid` | the resolved label MBID |
| `canonical_artist` | the resolved label name |
| `release_groups_json` | `LabelCacheEntry { version, label_name, releases: Vec<LabelRelease> }` |

`discography.cache_days` (30) is the TTL, a stale entry is refreshed, and a failed refresh falls back to the stale cache with the existing `DiscoveryProvenance::StaleCache` warning and the same circuit-breaker distinction (provider outage counts, a name that stopped resolving does not). A cached row whose stored MBID differs from the pinned or requested MBID is not compatible and is refetched.

`LabelRelease` is the serialisable unit: `{ release_id, release_group: ReleaseGroup, artist_credit: String }`, where `artist_credit` is the release's full credit string. Rows sharing a release-group ID collapse to one, keeping the earliest release date.

**Accepted limit:** a 30-day cache means a brand-new release can take up to 30 days to appear. That is the direct consequence of your cache choice; the spec records it rather than hiding it.

## 5. Work-list assembly

`src/label_discover.rs` is pure — no HTTP, no filesystem:

```rust
pub struct LabelTarget { pub artist: String, pub target: AlbumTarget }

pub fn label_targets(
    releases: Vec<LabelRelease>,
    allowed: &[DiscographyReleaseType],
    since: Option<PartialDate>,
    exclude_artists: &[String],
) -> LabelTargets   // { targets, counts }
```

1. **Credit filter** — an artist credit whose normalised key matches `discover.exclude_artists` is dropped and counted (`Various Artists`, `VA`, `Unknown Artist` by default). Your choice was to search under the full credit string, and that still holds for every non-excluded credit: `Nu:Tone feat. Stamina MC` is searched and staged as written.
2. **Type filter** — `release_allowed`, unchanged, so "studio albums" means the same thing in both sweeps.
3. **`--since` filter** — first-release-date at or after the bound. An **undated** release group cannot prove it satisfies the bound, so it is excluded and counted separately (`undated_skipped`), never silently admitted.
4. **Per-credit selection** — releases are grouped by normalised artist credit and each group goes through `select_albums(credit, groups, allowed)`, which reuses bundle decomposition, artist-prefix stripping and `album_identity_key` dedupe. Label mode therefore inherits every identity fix the artist sweep has.
5. **Cross-label merge** — targets from several labels merge and dedupe by `(artist key, album identity key)`; the first label in `--label` order owns a collision.
6. **Ordering** — deterministic and stable: artist key, then the existing dated-before-undated partial-date order, then normalised title, then release-group ID.
7. **Presence split** — `LibraryIndex::contains_album(artist, album)` separates present from missing, counted per class.

## 6. Download and placement

Missing targets go through `process_album(client, artist, Some(album), ignore_processed, config, db, staging_dir, progress, cancel, None, Some(LibraryTarget::StagingOnly))`, oldest first, charging the shared `discover.max_cycle_downloads` budget. `StagingOnly` already means "never create a library folder", so label mode writes **nothing** into `library.paths` — the album lands at `<storage.staging_dir>/<artist>/<album>/` via the existing nested staging layout, and the summary says so. `library.paths` is still required, because the presence check needs it (the mode-level check already enforces this).

## 7. Failure handling and reporting

- Per-label outcomes are independent: an unresolved label is reported and the run continues to the next label.
- `DISCOVER_PROVIDER_FAILURE_LIMIT` (3 consecutive MusicBrainz failures) aborts the run via the existing `abort_discover_run`, so a rate-limited API cannot spin through a whole label list.
- A scan failure warns and continues with an empty index (then every target is "missing" and goes to staging) — matching existing behaviour, not a silent skip.
- Cancellation is honoured between targets, and staging preparation is shared.
- New `LabelCounters` plus `label_notices()` mirror `discover_notices`, reporting: labels resolved/unresolved/provider-failed, releases examined, not-of-wanted-type, excluded credits, `--since` and undated exclusions, present-in-library, eligible, downloaded, staged, failed, and the budget stop point. No counter claims staging unless the outcome was actually `Downloaded { destination: Staging(_) }`.

## 8. Files touched

| File | Change |
|---|---|
| `src/discography/label.rs` (new) | `LabelInput`, `LabelCandidate`, `resolve_label`, `discover_label_releases` (cache + browse + guards), `LabelRelease`, `LabelCacheEntry`. |
| `src/discography/mod.rs` | Module wiring, `LabelUnresolved`/`LabelSearchInconsistent`, `DiscoveryFailure::from_error`, failure-cache predicate, shared partial-date type visibility. |
| `src/discography/musicbrainz.rs` | `label_search`, `label_by_id`, `releases_by_label` + wire types. |
| `src/label_discover.rs` (new) | Pure selection, `LabelTargets`, `LabelCounters`, `label_notices`. |
| `src/config.rs` | `discography.label_mbids` + validation; no new discover keys. |
| `src/mode.rs` | `--label`/`--release-type`/`--since` validation and `ExecutionPlan::Discover` fields. |
| `src/main.rs` | clap args, overrides plumbing, dispatch branch to `run_label_discover_mode`. |
| `src/runner.rs` | `run_label_discover_mode` + `_with_provider`; artist sweep untouched. |
| `src/lib.rs` | `pub mod label_discover;` |
| `tests/pipeline_test.rs` | One end-to-end label fixture: staged, library untouched. |

## 9. Testing

Unit: `LabelInput` parse/validate (including malformed UUID shapes); resolution dominance and ambiguity (mirroring the artist cases, driven by the real five-candidate Hospital Records shape); pagination guards (count drift, short page, duplicate IDs, over-limit); `label_targets` (type filter, `--since` boundary and undated exclusion, exclude-list, cross-label dedupe, ordering determinism); cache fresh/stale/refresh-failure/failure-replay/MBID mismatch.

Validation: every conflict and blank/unknown value above, one test each.

Integration (mock `DiscographyProvider` + mock Soulseek client): label run stages every album and writes nothing under `library.paths`; budget respected; unresolved label continues; three consecutive provider failures abort; summary notice text.

Gate: repo standard — TDD with genuine RED, cognitive complexity ≤ 25, clippy `-D warnings`, fmt, full suite, 95% line coverage floor.

## 10. Accepted limits, recorded in the spec

1. New releases surface at most `cache_days` (30) late.
2. The full official catalogue is paged per refresh because type filtering is client-side.
3. A release group that MusicBrainz has no artist credit for is skipped (counted), not guessed.
4. `--since` is a lower bound only; there is no upper bound and no "only the newest N".

## Goal

Let `--artist` carry an exact MusicBrainz identity — an ISNI, an IPI, or an
artist UUID — and fetch that artist's discography without adding new flags,
without weakening name resolution, and without guessing when a code matches more
than one artist.

## Scope

### In scope

- Value-shape detection on the existing `--artist` flag.
- A provider search path for IPI and ISNI; the existing MBID lookup for UUIDs.
- Strict single-carrier resolution with candidate self-verification.
- Discover mode and artist-only manual mode.
- The resolved canonical name as the work item's name.
- Cache keys, the `discography.artist_mbids` interaction, observability, docs.

### Out of scope

- Reading MusicBrainz IDs from file tags. The library scanner captures artist,
  album and bitrate only, so presence, placement and the folder gate stay
  name-based; identity matching against the library is not part of this design.
- New configuration keys. `discography.artist_mbids` keeps UUID values; only its
  keys gain the ability to be a code.
- Identifiers in the automatic sweep or in `discover.exclude_artists`, which are
  library-derived and name-keyed.
- Identifiers in `--mode manual --album Y` runs and in `--batch-file` lines,
  which never ask MusicBrainz.
- Supplying more than one identifier for a single run.
- `arid:` search for UUIDs: an entity lookup already exists and is exact.

## Decisions

### The existing flag carries the identifier, and its shape decides

`--artist` stays a single `Option<String>`; no flag is added. Auto-detection was
chosen over explicit `--artist-ipi`/`--artist-isni` flags because the whole point
is to be simpler than editing configuration, and over a config-only extension
because a one-off run should not need a config edit. Accepted cost: a band
literally named like one of the code shapes would be read as a code. The escape
hatch is the existing `discography.artist_mbids` pin, which takes precedence over
the input's own shape (see Caching and pins).

### One value per run

Supplying a name *and* a code together is not supported: the code alone is
strictly more precise, so there is nothing to combine, and a precedence rule
would be one more thing to document, test and get wrong.

### Exactly one carrier, or refuse

A candidate counts only if its own `ipis`/`isnis` array contains the requested
code. Zero carriers and several carriers are both refusals, reported distinctly.
An IPI or ISNI is not unique by construction — a person and a group, or two
MusicBrainz entities for one act, can share one — and the existing dominance
rules cannot help because MusicBrainz scores identifier hits at or near 100
regardless of which artist they are. Refusing is also consistent with the hard
error an unresolvable name already raises before the walk.

### Codes are honoured where a discography is fetched

Discover mode and artist-only manual mode both accept a code, matching how
`discography.artist_mbids` already applies to both. Paths that never ask
MusicBrainz — `--mode manual --artist X --album Y` and batch lines — reject a
recognisable identifier with a configuration error, because a code cannot name a
library folder and searching Soulseek for a digit string fails late and
confusingly.

### A code-only run names the work item after the resolved artist

The work item carries the canonical MusicBrainz name of the artist that owns the
code. Library folder lookup, the `Artist Album` search, placement and the
processed records then follow today's rules unchanged: the on-disk folder
spelling wins when the library already holds a folder for that artist, otherwise
the existing staging fallback and warning apply. A code run behaves exactly like a
run naming that canonical name, except the identity came from the code.

### IPI and ISNI get a provider search; UUIDs reuse the entity lookup

A new `search_artists_by_identifier` covers IPI and ISNI, keeping MusicBrainz
query syntax inside the HTTP layer where it lives today. A UUID needs no search:
`artist_by_id` is an exact entity lookup and is more reliable than an `arid:`
query. The existing heavily tested `search_artists(name)` path is untouched.

## CLI surface

| `--artist` value, after stripping spaces and hyphens | Treated as | Validation |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `8-4-4-4-12` hexadecimal UUID | MusicBrainz artist ID | the existing `valid_mbid` rules |
| 16 characters, digits with an optional trailing `X` | ISNI | ISO 7064 MOD 11-2 check digit |
| 11 digits | IPI | digits only; IPI has no check digit |
| anything else | artist name | today's behaviour, unchanged |

A value that looks like a code but fails validation — a bad ISNI check digit, 15
or 12 digits, a UUID with the wrong group lengths — is a configuration error
naming the problem. It is not silently searched for as a name, and it does not
claim the artist is unknown. This is the only change in behaviour for a
name-shaped input.

IPIs carry no check digit, so a mistyped but well-formed IPI surfaces as "no
MusicBrainz artist carries this IPI" rather than as a validation error.

## Provider layer

- `ArtistIdentifier { Isni(String), Ipi(String) }`, held normalised: digits only
  for both, with an ISNI check character upper-cased. Parsing and normalisation
  are pure functions shared by the CLI validation, the resolver and the cache key.
- `DiscographyProvider` gains
  `search_artists_by_identifier(&self, &ArtistIdentifier) -> Result<Vec<ArtistCandidate>, DiscographyError>`.
  The implementation builds `isni:"…"` or `ipi:"…"` and reuses the existing
  request, pacing, retry, `offset != 0` and count-versus-payload consistency
  checks verbatim, so an identifier search classifies its failures exactly as a
  name search does.
- `ArtistWire` gains `#[serde(default)] ipis`, `isnis` and `disambiguation`.
  `ArtistCandidate` gains the two identifier lists so the resolver can verify a
  candidate; `disambiguation` is carried for reporting.
- Test fixtures that construct `ArtistCandidate` gain two empty vectors. This is
  mechanical and is the accepted cost of keeping one candidate type rather than a
  parallel identifier-only type.

<!-- markdownlint-disable MD013 -->

# Label-based discovery

## Problem

`discover` mode can only work out what to download from the library it is given: it
indexes the audio files on disk, derives an artist list from tags and folder names,
asks MusicBrainz for each artist's discography, and fills the gaps. The operator has no
way to say "I want whatever this record label has released", so a whole class of
acquisition is unsupported: a label's roster is exactly the set of artists an operator
does not yet know about, and an artist the library has never seen can never enter the
work list.

The request is to sweep a record label - concrete example: Hospital Records - and pick
up every release of a wanted type (studio albums by default) that the library does not
hold, using MusicBrainz as the authority for what the label has released.

Two facts about the provider shape this design:

- MusicBrainz exposes **no** browse of release groups by label. The only label-keyed
  path is browsing **releases** (`/ws/2/release?label=<mbid>`), whose payload carries
  each release's release group inline when `inc=release-groups` is requested. Label
  discovery therefore starts from releases rather than from release groups, and
  collapses to release groups locally.
- Label names are ambiguous in practice. A live query for
  `label:"Hospital Records"` returns five candidates - score 100 for the UK drum &
  bass label (label code 12939) and score 62 for a US noisecore label - so a label
  needs the same "resolve safely or refuse" treatment `--artist` already has.

## Goal

Let `--label` name one or more record labels on a `discover` run, resolve each label to
exactly one MusicBrainz entity or refuse, fetch every release of the wanted type on
that label, and download the ones the library does not hold into staging - without
changing anything about the existing library-derived artist sweep.

## Scope

### In scope

- A `--label` flag on `discover` mode accepting a label name or a MusicBrainz label
  MBID, comma-delimited and repeatable within one value list.
- Label resolution with the existing dominance rules, plus pinning via a new
  `discography.label_mbids` map.
- Browsing a label's releases, with pagination guards, a hard catalogue ceiling, and
  30-day caching in the existing `discography_cache` table.
- `--release-type` as a per-run override of `discography.allowed_types`.
- `--since` as an optional lower bound on a release group's first-release-date.
- Selection of missing albums by artist credit, reuse of `release_allowed`,
  `select_albums` and `album_identity_key`.
- Staging-only placement for every label-sourced download.
- Run-summary counters and notices, failure caching, and the provider circuit breaker.
- Documentation and end-to-end coverage.

### Out of scope

- Writing label-sourced albums into `library.paths`. Label runs never create an artist
  folder; the operator moves albums out of staging.
- Browsing by label series, imprint, sub-label or distributor. A label is one
  MusicBrainz label entity.
- Following a label's roster as a subscription: an artist is only ever discovered
  through a release that is on the label and of the wanted type.
- Release-level (as opposed to release-group-level) selection, format preferences,
  country, barcode and catalog-number handling.
- New `discover` configuration keys. The run-time selectors live on the execution
  plan, so nothing about a label run is persisted except its cache row and any
  recorded resolution failure.
- A date upper bound, "newest N" windows, and notification of newly released albums
  outside a run.
- Supplying `--artist` and `--label` together, or combining a label sweep with the
  library sweep in one invocation.

## Decisions

### One flag carries the label, and its shape decides

`--label` takes a label name or a MusicBrainz label MBID, detected by value shape.
This mirrors `--artist`, which already accepts a name, an IPI, an ISNI or an artist
MBID in one flag, and keeps the CLI surface to one new option. Two flags
(`--label` plus `--label-id`) and a name-only flag were both considered: the first
adds a second validation surface for no expressive gain, the second cannot express an
ambiguous label at all.

Accepted cost: a label literally named like a UUID would be read as an MBID. The
escape hatch is `discography.label_mbids`, which pins by name and wins over the input's
own shape.

### A comma-delimited list, swept in one run

`--label` is `value_delimiter = ','` and merges several labels into one work list, the
way `--library-path` already accepts a list. One invocation covers a label family
(Hospital Records plus Med School), which is what an operator actually wants when they
start curating by label, and a single shared download budget keeps the run bounded.

Consequences, made explicit rather than inferred: labels are resolved in the order
given, targets are merged and de-duplicated across labels, and a target reachable from
two labels is owned by the first label that produced it.

### A label run replaces the library sweep

When `--label` is present the run's work list is the label catalogue alone. The
library is still scanned, because "already present" cannot be answered without it, but
its artists never enter the work list. Mixing the two sources would make a run's cost
and its summary depend on two very different inputs, and the shared download budget
(`discover.max_cycle_downloads`) would let the library sweep consume the budget before
the label was reached.

`--artist` and `--label` together are refused: an explicitly named artist is a
single-artist request, a label is a catalogue request, and neither is a filter on the
other.

### The wanted type comes from config, overridable per run

Label runs honour `discography.allowed_types` (default `[studio_album]`) exactly as the
artist sweep does, and `--release-type` overrides it for one run. This keeps one
classifier - `release_allowed` - and one vocabulary - the `DiscographyReleaseType`
enum - across both sweeps, while letting "albums and EPs" be a command-line decision
rather than a config edit.

Two alternatives were rejected. Config-only would force a config edit for a one-off
run. A required-per-run `--release-type` would make label runs ignore the
`discography` section that governs every other MusicBrainz query, which is a silent
inconsistency waiting to be reported as a bug.

`album` is accepted as an alias of `studio_album`, because an operator asking for
"albums" means exactly what `StudioAlbum` classifies; `release_allowed` already treats
an `Album` primary type with no secondary types as a studio album. Both spellings map
to the same enum variant, so the alias cannot diverge from the classifier.

### "New" means missing from the library, optionally bounded by `--since`

The default is gap-fill, matching the artist sweep: every album of the wanted type on
the label that the library does not hold. A rolling recency window as the default was
rejected because it silently never fetches a label's back catalogue and because a
missed run longer than the window would lose releases permanently.

`--since YYYY[-MM[-DD]]` bounds a first run or a backfill without changing the
definition of missing. It is a lower bound on the release group's first-release-date,
validated by the same partial-date rules used for MusicBrainz dates. An **undated**
release group cannot satisfy a lower bound it cannot prove, so it is excluded and
counted separately; it is never admitted on the assumption that it is recent.

### The artist credit is the searchable artist, verbatim

A label-sourced album is searched and staged under the release's full artist credit as
MusicBrainz spells it (`Nu:Tone feat. Stamina MC`), not under a stripped lead artist.
The credit is what identifies the release, the library's own tags use the same shape,
and trimming it would make the Soulseek query differ from the album's identity on disk.

`discover.exclude_artists` still applies: a credit whose normalised key matches an
excluded name (`Various Artists`, `VA`, `Unknown Artist` by default) is dropped and
counted. This reuses an existing, documented key rather than introducing a label-only
exclusion list.

### Every label-sourced download stays in staging

Label runs pass `LibraryTarget::StagingOnly` to `process_album`. That variant already
documents itself as "the album stays in staging: nothing is written to the library,
because placement has no artist folder to write into and never creates one", so no new
placement code is needed and no label run can create a library folder.

Creating `<library.paths[0]>/<Artist>/<Album>/` was considered and rejected by the
operator: the value of the feature is discovery, not unattended writes into the
library, and the operator moves albums deliberately.

### Cache the catalogue for the configured discography TTL

The label catalogue is cached in `discography_cache` under a namespaced key with the
same `discography.cache_days` (30) lifetime and the same stale-on-refresh-failure
behaviour as an artist discography. No schema change: `artist_key` is a
`TEXT PRIMARY KEY COLLATE NOCASE`, so `label:<normalised name>` is a key, and the
label path is the only reader of that prefix.

Accepted consequence: a brand-new release can take up to 30 days to appear in a sweep.
That is the direct cost of the chosen lifetime; a shorter label-only TTL was rejected
as one more configuration surface for a modest gain, and no-cache was rejected as
re-fetching up to 12 pages every run.

### Resolution refuses rather than guesses

Label resolution reuses the constants and shape of artist resolution: exactly one
canonical exact-name match is accepted; duplicates require every candidate to carry a
score, exactly one candidate at `REQUIRED_TOP_SCORE`, and a lead of at least
`REQUIRED_SCORE_MARGIN`. Anything else is `LabelUnresolved` with the candidates in the
message, so the operator can pin the right MBID instead of discovering later that the
run downloaded from the wrong label.

## CLI surface

| Flag | Values | Validation |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--label` | one or more label names or label MBIDs, comma-delimited | discover mode only; each element non-blank; a UUID shape must pass `valid_mbid`; duplicates after normalisation are refused; refused together with `--artist`, `--album` and `--batch-file` |
| `--release-type` | `studio_album`, `album` (alias), `live_album`, `ep`, `single`, `compilation`, `remix`, `soundtrack`, `dj_mix`, `mixtape` | requires `--label`; unknown value refuses and lists the accepted set; an empty list refuses |
| `--since` | `YYYY`, `YYYY-MM` or `YYYY-MM-DD` | requires `--label`; must parse under the partial-date rules; a partial date lower-bounds by its missing components (a `YYYY-MM` bound sorts before any day in that month) |

Every new refusal names the flag and the reason, in the existing style, for example
`--artist and --label are mutually exclusive; run one source per invocation` and
`--release-type is only valid with --label`.

The validated selectors ride on the execution plan, not on `Config`:

```rust
pub enum ExecutionPlan {
    // ...
    Discover {
        /// The one explicitly named artist, when the operator named one.
        artist: Option<String>,
        /// Labels to sweep; empty means the library-derived artist sweep.
        labels: Vec<LabelRequest>,
        /// Per-run override of `discography.allowed_types`.
        release_types: Option<Vec<DiscographyReleaseType>>,
        /// Per-run lower bound on a release group's first-release-date.
        since: Option<PartialDate>,
    },
}
```

`LabelRequest` is the parsed `--label` element: `{ input: String, mbid: Option<String> }`,
so the runner never re-parses a CLI string and the mode layer owns shape validation.

## Config surface

One new key, shaped exactly like the map it sits beside:

```yaml
discography:
  label_mbids:
    "Hospital Records": 8562598d-60d1-4bd6-8b85-4d709e951770
```

Validation, shared with `artist_mbids` through the same helper: a key must not be
empty, two keys must not collide after normalisation, and every value must be a valid
MusicBrainz MBID.

## Provider layer

`src/discography/label.rs` mirrors `src/discography/identifier.rs`.

- `LabelInput::parse(&str) -> LabelInput` classifies `Mbid` or `Name`; `validate()`
  returns the malformed-shape reason for a UUID that does not pass `valid_mbid`;
  `pin_key()` normalises a configured name for map lookup; `cache_key()` returns the
  `label:` namespaced key.
- `LabelCandidate { id, name, score: Option<u8>, disambiguation: Option<String>, label_code: Option<u32> }`.
  `label_code` and `disambiguation` exist to make an ambiguity message actionable.
- `DiscographyProvider` gains two methods, both required rather than defaulted, so a
  provider that quietly returned nothing cannot look like a label with no releases:

```rust
async fn search_labels(&self, label: &str) -> Result<Vec<LabelCandidate>, DiscographyError>;
async fn label_by_id(&self, label_mbid: &str) -> Result<LabelCandidate, DiscographyError>;
async fn releases_by_label(&self, label_mbid: &str) -> Result<Vec<LabelRelease>, DiscographyError>;
```

`MusicBrainzProvider` implements them with the existing request plumbing - pacing,
`Retry-After`/503 pauses, the 4 MiB body cap, transport and decode classification - so
a label query fails exactly as an artist query does.

Wire types:

- `LabelSearchPage { count, offset, labels: Vec<LabelWire> }` with
  `#[serde(rename = "label-count")]` / `#[serde(rename = "label-offset")]` if the
  response carries them, otherwise honest `Option`s.
- `ReleasePage { count, offset, releases: Vec<ReleaseWire> }` renamed from
  `release-count` / `release-offset`.
- `ReleaseWire { id, title, date, status, release_group: Option<ReleaseGroupWire>, artist_credit: Vec<ArtistCreditWire> }`,
  where `ArtistCreditWire { name, joinphrase }` is flattened into the credit string by
  the same `credit_name()` helper the artist path uses for candidate names, so
  `Nu:Tone feat. Stamina MC` is produced by concatenation of names and joinphrases
  rather than by guesswork.

`LabelRelease`, the unit both the provider and the selector use:

```rust
pub struct LabelRelease {
    pub release_id: String,
    pub release_group: ReleaseGroup,
    /// The full credit string, as MusicBrainz spells it.
    pub artist_credit: String,
}
```

A release whose payload has no release group or no artist credit is dropped in the
provider and counted by the caller as `skipped_incomplete`; it is never reconstructed
by guessing an artist or a title.

## Catalogue retrieval

```
GET /ws/2/release
  ?label=<mbid>
  &status=official
  &inc=release-groups
  &fmt=json
  &limit=100
  &offset=<offset>
```

- `status=official` is sent server-side: it removes bootlegs and promotional copies
  without a client-side guess.
- `type` is deliberately **not** sent. Browse type filtering cannot express secondary
  types (`live`, `compilation`, `remix`, `soundtrack`, `dj mix`, `mixtape`), so
  sending it for some type sets and not others would make the server and
  `release_allowed` two sources of truth. Measured cost on the real label: 1137
  official releases (12 pages) instead of 397 with `type=album` (4 pages), paid once
  per cache lifetime.
- Pagination guards mirror `release_groups` exactly: first page must report offset 0,
  each page's `release-count` must equal the first page's, each page's length must
  equal `min(remaining, PAGE_SIZE)`, no page may contain a duplicate release ID, and
  the collected total must equal the reported count. Any violation is
  `DiscographyError::IncompletePagination` and the cache is not written: a partial
  catalogue looks exactly like "nothing new" and must never be treated as complete.
- `MAX_LABEL_RELEASES` (5000) caps a catalogue that exceeds what one sweep can
  responsibly page through; exceeding it is `IncompletePagination` naming the count.

## Caching and pins

| `discography_cache` column | Value for a label row |
| --- | --- |
| `artist_key` | `label:<pin_key(label)>` |
| `artist_mbid` | the resolved label MBID |
| `canonical_artist` | the resolved label name |
| `release_groups_json` | `LabelCacheEntry { version, label_name, releases: Vec<LabelRelease> }` |
| `fetched_at` | unchanged |

Read path: a fresh row is served as `DiscoveryProvenance::FreshCache`; a stale row is
refreshed; a failed refresh that produced a usable stale row is served as
`DiscoveryProvenance::StaleCache` with a warning naming age and reason. A cached row
whose stored MBID differs from the pinned or requested MBID is not compatible and is
refetched, so a pin change takes effect immediately.

Write path: only after a complete, validated catalogue, and only when
`discography.cache_days > 0`; the payload is size-checked against
`MAX_CACHE_PAYLOAD_BYTES` before insert.

Failure caching: `LabelUnresolved` is recorded in `discography_failures` under
`label:<pin_key>` with `failure_kind = "unresolved"` and honoured for
`discography.failure_cache_days`. `LabelSearchInconsistent` is deliberately **not**
cached - it describes one inconsistent response, not a property of the name.

## Resolution

1. A `discography.label_mbids` pin wins over the input's shape and is fetched by ID.
2. An MBID-shaped input is fetched by ID.
3. A name is searched with `label:"<escaped name>"`; the query is built in the HTTP
   layer, so Lucene syntax never leaves it.
4. The candidates are classified by canonical exact-name match under
   `normalize_catalog_key`; one match is accepted, several are accepted only under the
   dominance rule, zero is refused.
5. A refusal names up to `MAX_LISTED_LABELS` (10) candidates with score, label code
   and disambiguation, so pinning the intended one is a copy-paste away.

## Data flow

```text
--label "Hospital Records,Med School"
  -> mode layer: parse, validate, build ExecutionPlan::Discover
  -> runner: prepare staging, open provider
  -> for each label (in given order)
       resolve label            (pin | by-id | search + dominance)   [cached failure honoured]
       load catalogue           (fresh cache | browse + guards | stale cache) [30-day TTL]
       collect LabelRelease list
  -> label_targets(releases, allowed_types, since, exclude_artists)
       drop excluded credits
       release_allowed
       since bound (undated excluded and counted)
       group by normalised artist credit
       select_albums per credit group  (bundle split, identity dedupe, ordering)
       merge across labels, dedupe by (artist key, album identity key)
       deterministic ordering
  -> library scan (index_from_paths) -> LibraryIndex
  -> split present / missing
  -> for each missing target, oldest first
       process_album(..., LibraryTarget::StagingOnly)
       charge DownloadBudget on a download charge
  -> label_notices -> RunReport
```

## Selection detail

`src/label_discover.rs` is pure: it takes `Vec<LabelRelease>`, the allowed types, the
optional `since` bound and the exclusion list, and returns targets plus counters. It
performs no I/O, so every filter and ordering rule is unit-testable without HTTP or a
filesystem.

`select_albums(credit, groups, allowed)` is reused per artist-credit group rather than
reimplemented for labels. That gives label mode the existing bundle decomposition,
artist-prefix stripping and `album_identity_key` collapsing for free - the label path
cannot drift from the artist path on what counts as one album.

Ordering is total and deterministic: artist key, then the existing partial-date order
(dated before undated, earlier first), then normalised title, then release-group ID.
Two runs over the same catalogue therefore download in the same order, which is what
makes a budget-limited sweep converge instead of oscillating.

## Download and placement

- Every target is processed as `process_album(client, artist, Some(&album), ignore_processed, ..., Some(LibraryTarget::StagingOnly))`.
  The album lands at `<storage.staging_dir>/<artist>/<album>/` via the nested staging
  layout, and nothing is written under `library.paths`.
- `discover.max_cycle_downloads` bounds the run; the loop stops at the same points as
  the artist sweep (budget exhausted, cancellation), recording the artist it stopped on.
- `discover.ignore_processed` and `--ignore-processed` behave as they do for an
  artist-only run: a recorded success is skipped unless the flag bypasses it.
- Every album is charged exactly as an artist-sweep album is (`charges_download_budget`
  on success, `charges_after_error` on failure), so the budget cannot be gamed by
  failed attempts.

## Error handling

| Situation | Behaviour | Reported as |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Malformed UUID shape in `--label` or `label_mbids` | refuse before any request | configuration error naming the flag |
| Label name resolves to no exact match, or ambiguous candidates | skip that label, continue with the remaining labels | `unresolved` list plus a `discography_failures` row |
| Label search response internally inconsistent | skip that label, do not cache the failure | `unresolved` list, uncached |
| Transport, 5xx, decode, oversized body, pagination guard | skip that label | `provider_failed`, counted by the circuit breaker |
| Catalogue exceeds `MAX_LABEL_RELEASES` | skip that label, do not cache a partial catalogue | `provider_failed` with the limit named |
| Three consecutive provider failures | abort the run through the existing `abort_discover_run` | `SeakarrError::MusicBrainz`, as today |
| Library scan fails | warn, continue with an empty index, so every target is treated as missing | warning plus the existing notices |
| Library scan cancelled | stop before any download | cancelled notice, as today |
| No label resolves at all | finish the run with an explanatory notice | notice, exit success |

An unresolved label never counts towards the circuit breaker, and a provider failure
never writes a failure-cache row: the two failure classes stay separate, exactly as
`DiscoveryFailure` already separates them for artists.

## Observability

`LabelCounters` and `label_notices()` mirror `DiscoverCounters`/`discover_notices`,
in this order:

1. Labels resolved, with the resolved names and MBIDs.
2. Labels unresolved, listed; pin advice when more than one is unresolved.
3. Labels whose provider request failed, with reasons.
4. Releases examined, and how many were dropped as not of the wanted type.
5. Releases dropped by `--since`, and releases dropped as undated under `--since`.
6. Releases dropped because their artist credit is excluded.
7. Albums already present in the library.
8. Albums eligible this run.
9. Albums downloaded and staged; albums failed, with reasons.
10. The budget stop point, when the budget ended the run.
11. A closing line stating that staged albums were not written to the library, naming
    `storage.staging_dir`, so the placement rule is never a surprise.

No counter claims staging unless the outcome was
`AlbumOutcome::Downloaded { destination: DownloadDestination::Staging(_) }`, matching
the artist sweep's honesty rule.

## Components and boundaries

| File | Responsibility after this change |
| --- | --- |
| `src/discography/label.rs` (new) | Label identity (`LabelInput`, `LabelCandidate`), resolution, catalogue retrieval with guards, cache read/write, `LabelRelease` and `LabelCacheEntry`. Depends on the provider and the database; knows nothing about download or placement. |
| `src/discography/mod.rs` | Declares `pub mod label;`. Adds `LabelUnresolved` and `LabelSearchInconsistent`; extends `DiscoveryFailure::from_error` and the failure-cache predicate; makes `PartialDate` and `parse_partial_date` `pub(crate)` so `mode.rs` can validate `--since` with the same rules. |
| `src/discography/musicbrainz.rs` | `search_labels`, `label_by_id`, `releases_by_label`, their wire types, and the label/release response parsers. |
| `src/label_discover.rs` (new) | Pure selection (`label_targets`), `LabelTargets`, `LabelCounters`, `label_notices`. Depends only on `discography` types and `LibraryIndex`. |
| `src/config.rs` | `discography.label_mbids` with validation shared with `artist_mbids`. |
| `src/mode.rs` | `--label`/`--release-type`/`--since` parsing and validation; `ExecutionPlan::Discover` gains `labels`, `release_types`, `since`; `LabelRequest`. |
| `src/main.rs` | clap arguments (both `value_delimiter = ','`), override plumbing, dispatch of a label plan to `run_label_discover_mode`. |
| `src/runner.rs` | `run_label_discover_mode` (staging preparation, provider construction) and `run_label_discover_mode_with_provider` (resolve, fetch, select, download, report). The library sweep path is untouched. |
| `src/lib.rs` | `pub mod label_discover;` |

Boundary rules: the provider module owns HTTP and cache; `label_discover` owns filters
and ordering; `runner` owns sequencing and side effects; `mode` owns validation. Each
can be tested without the other, and none of the four grows a second responsibility.

## Testing

Unit - `LabelInput`: name, MBID, malformed UUID, blank, comma-splitting, duplicate
detection after normalisation, pin-key normalisation.

Unit - resolution: single exact match; ambiguous with dominance; ambiguous with tied
top score; top score below `REQUIRED_TOP_SCORE`; margin below `REQUIRED_SCORE_MARGIN`;
zero matches; a pinned MBID winning over a name; `label_by_id` skipping search
entirely. The five-candidate `Hospital Records` shape is a fixture.

Unit - provider: page parsing, `release-count`/`release-offset` handling, missing
release group dropped, multi-part artist credit joined (`names` plus `joinphrase`),
first-page offset not zero, count drift between pages, short page, duplicate release
IDs, `MAX_LABEL_RELEASES` exceeded, 4 MiB body cap, 503 with `Retry-After`.

Unit - cache: fresh hit, stale refresh, stale served on refresh failure, failure
replay, failure bypass for a pinned MBID, MBID mismatch refetched, oversized payload
rejected.

Unit - selection: type filter per variant; `album` alias equals `studio_album`;
`--since` inclusive boundary at year, month and day precision; undated excluded under
`--since` and counted; undated admitted without `--since`; excluded credits dropped;
two labels producing one album collapse to one target; cross-artist identity
collapsing; deterministic ordering across shuffled input.

Validation - every refusal in the CLI table, one test each, asserting the message names
the flag.

Integration (mock provider and mock Soulseek client): a label run stages every eligible
album and leaves `library.paths` byte-identical; a present album is skipped; the budget
stops the run at the configured number; an unresolved label does not stop the run; three
consecutive provider failures abort with the existing error; the summary carries the
staging notice.

End-to-end (`tests/pipeline_test.rs`): one label fixture through `--mode discover
--label ... --release-type album`, asserting the staged tree and that no library folder
was created.

Gate: TDD with a genuine RED phase, cognitive complexity ceiling 25, `cargo clippy
--all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --check`, the full test suite, the repository's
95% line-coverage floor, `cargo audit`, `cargo deny`, and the pre-commit hooks.

## Documentation

- `README.md`: the discover bullet gains the label sweep - `--label`, the name-or-MBID
  rule, `--release-type`, `--since`, staging-only placement, the 30-day cache, and the
  fact that a label run replaces the library sweep for that invocation.
- `README.md` configuration reference: `discography.label_mbids`.
- The flag table and the mode/selector compatibility table list the three new flags and
  the `--label` conflicts.

## Accepted consequences

1. A newly released album can take up to `discography.cache_days` (30) to appear in a
   sweep, and a pause between runs longer than the cache lifetime is served from a
   refresh rather than from the stale row.
2. The full official catalogue is paged on a cold or stale cache (12 pages for the
   example label), because type filtering stays client-side.
3. A release group MusicBrainz has no artist credit for is skipped and counted, never
   attributed by guesswork.
4. `--since` is a lower bound only; there is no upper bound and no "newest N" selector.
5. A label whose catalogue exceeds `MAX_LABEL_RELEASES` cannot be swept until the
   ceiling is raised deliberately in code.
6. Multi-artist credits produce multi-artist staging folders, which the operator may
   need to merge by hand.
7. Label discovery cannot see an artist that has no release of the wanted type on the
   label, even if the label has signed them.

## Acceptance criteria

1. `seakarr --mode discover --label "Hospital Records"` resolves that label to the
   MusicBrainz entity for the UK drum & bass label, or refuses with candidates listed;
   it never silently picks a lower-scored namesake.
2. `--label` with an MBID performs no label search request.
3. `--release-type ep` downloads EPs only; omitting the flag downloads
   `discography.allowed_types`.
4. `--since 2025-01-01` excludes release groups first released before that date and
   excludes undated ones, both counted in the summary.
5. Every label-sourced download is present under
   `<storage.staging_dir>/<artist>/<album>/` and nothing is written under
   `library.paths`.
6. An album already in the library is not searched, not downloaded, and is counted as
   present.
7. `--label` and `--artist` together refuse with a message naming both flags; so do
   `--release-type` and `--since` without `--label`.
8. Three consecutive MusicBrainz provider failures abort the run through the existing
   breaker; an unresolvable label does not.
9. A second run inside `discography.cache_days` makes no catalogue request and reports
   the fresh-cache provenance.
10. The library-derived artist sweep behaves exactly as before when `--label` is
    absent: same selection, same notices, same placement.

## Catalogue retrieval

```
GET /ws/2/release
  ?label=<mbid>
  &status=official
  &inc=release-groups
  &fmt=json
  &limit=100
  &offset=<offset>
```

- `status=official` is sent server-side: it removes bootlegs and promotional copies
  without a client-side guess.
- `type` is deliberately **not** sent. Browse type filtering cannot express secondary
  types (`live`, `compilation`, `remix`, `soundtrack`, `dj mix`, `mixtape`), so
  sending it for some type sets and not others would make the server and
  `release_allowed` two sources of truth. Measured cost on the real label: 1137
  official releases (12 pages) instead of 397 with `type=album` (4 pages), paid once
  per cache lifetime.
- Pagination guards mirror `release_groups` exactly: first page must report offset 0,
  each page's `release-count` must equal the first page's, each page's length must
  equal `min(remaining, PAGE_SIZE)`, no page may contain a duplicate release ID, and
  the collected total must equal the reported count. Any violation is
  `DiscographyError::IncompletePagination` and the cache is not written: a partial
  catalogue looks exactly like "nothing new" and must never be treated as complete.
- `MAX_LABEL_RELEASES` (5000) caps a catalogue that exceeds what one sweep can
  responsibly page through; exceeding it is `IncompletePagination` naming the count.

content.text:
Spec written, linted and committed to `docs/agent/specs/2026-11-01-label-based-discovery-design.md` (`markdownlint` clean, 560 lines, HEAD `0ba3d99`).

**Self-review applied** — six fixes, all inline:

1. `http` language added to the fenced request block (MD040).
2. `// ...` in the `ExecutionPlan` snippet replaced with explicit "existing variants are unchanged".
3. "gains two methods" corrected to three (`search_labels`, `label_by_id`, `releases_by_label`).
4. Observability gained the incomplete-release count (payload with no release group or no artist credit), which the provider section already required.
5. Accepted-consequence 1 reworded — it had conflated cache expiry with refresh failure.
